utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the Registrar call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number, IT-95-8/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Dusan Fustar, Predrag Banovic, and Dusko Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Appearances.

utterances.speaker: MS. BODSON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, for the Keraterm case, Skye Winner, who is the case manager, Sureta Chana, as Prosecution counsel. My name is Bodson, I am the lead counsel in this case, and we are also assisted for this hearing by Ms. Joanna Korner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, and for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: My name is Theodore Scudder, and I am here on behalf of the defendant, Dusan Fustar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Tom Moran, Your Honour, I'm appointed to represent Mr. Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Jovan Babic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphone was off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The microphone was off for the last counsel. Please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Jovan Babic. I am representing Predrag Banovic in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. We have a number of matters to consider. And to the extent that we can decide, I have a list that I will go through. The information which I'll give is largely based on the preparatory meetings held between the senior legal officer and counsel. I may call on particular counsel, but if I don't, and either counsel has a matter to raise, feel free to raise it. The first matter is the amendment of the indictment and the motion for joinder. Many matters rest on the resolution of this, and I am to say that the Trial Chamber will be giving a decision on this within the next two weeks. We will not have any oral argument on this. The second matter is the filing of the pretrial brief. Dates have been set, and those dates were vacated because it was more sensible to await the determination of the question of joinder. So right now, we are not in a position to set new dates. But I would like to give an indicative date, assuming that the decision is given on joinder within the next two weeks, then it seems to me that the Prosecutor would have some two months after the joinder decision, which would take us into mid-November, and the Defence one month after that, to the end of January. This is only indicative, and we must await definitive dates following the decision on joinder. The question of disclosure, witness statements, under Rule 66 (A) (i), all statements have been disclosed in both English and B/C/S without redaction, and the Prosecution filed a notice of compliance with Rule 66 (A)(i) on the 25th of July with respect of Knezevic, the last accused to be brought into custody, and copies of all supporting materials that accompanied the second amended indictment were disclosed to counsel of the accused. Rule 66 (A)(ii), at the last Status Conference, the Prosecutor was granted an extension of time until the 15th of June to comply with its obligation. And the request was granted. So I'd like to hear from the Prosecutor whether she has discharged that duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. BODSON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. As regards the accused Fustar and Banovic, we have fulfilled this obligation; in particular, the accused -- these accused have received copies of statements of 20 witnesses out of 27 who will be called by the Prosecution. That concerns both Rule 66 and 68. Also, curriculum vitae of expert witnesses and expert witness reports in form of written statements pursuant to Rules -- to the relevant Rules, also statements of Mr. Clark and Weiss [phoen] have also been disclosed. We have a problem concerning the defence of the accused Knezevic. He has been assigned a counsel, Mr. Moran, whose mandate is limited, and will expire in two weeks, as far as I know. We have transmitted to Mr. Knezevic the documents pursuant to Rule 66 (A)(i), but for the last part, we have to transmit five binders who are here behind me, and we would like to hear from Mr. Moran to whom we should disclose these documents and by what date. We have not received any response to this date, but we would like to know how to proceed so that the three accused can be given simultaneously the same documents. As regards the remainder of the evidence to be disclosed, we are still inquiring about the six remaining witnesses, and we expect to finish this job on the 15th of September, which will enable us to disclose the remaining evidence by late November, subject to any problems that may arise. We have also received 19 out of 24 translations of the remaining documents who are to be transmitted to the Defence. We are still waiting for these translations to be given to us. As regards the seven new witnesses that I have mentioned a moment ago, there are still translations pending, and that will also be disclosed as soon as its finished. As regards the problem concerning the transcript of the case Keraterm I, these transcripts have been provided to the Defence in English. We are in the process of receiving B/C/S translations of these transcripts. And as soon as we have everything together, the entire material will be disclosed to the Defence. I think that that concludes what I had to say in respect of the disclosure of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You have really given us a rundown of your entire list of duties. I still intend to go through the matters individually. One issue that was raised relates to Mr. Moran.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I understand that your assignment will be extended. Now, I know that there is a pending motion, and that is going to be determined by the Chamber as soon as possible. But my information that I have just received from the Registrar is that your assignment will be extended.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have been orally informed of that. I have not seen the decision yet, but I'm sure that it's coming from OLAD. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's the accused --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Knezevic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Knezevic. Do you want to say something, Mr. Knezevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please, Your Honour. Let me first bid good afternoon to everybody present in the courtroom. I do not want to take too much of your time. I do not wish Mr. Moran to represent me before this International Tribunal. I have not given him my power of attorney. I have given this document to another person, another lawyer, whom I wish to represent me. I do not want any misunderstanding or any problems, and that was the reason why I wanted to address the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Knezevic. As I just indicated, the Chamber is seised of the motion that you have filed relating to this matter. And the Chamber will be making a decision on this issue within the shortest time. Going down my list, experts, the four experts, and my information is that all expert reports have been obtained, translated, and transmitted to the Defence. Exhibits, according to the OTP, there are about 30 exhibits. And the OTP has been advised that these will have to be disclosed, copies provided in B/C/S with the pretrial brief. And the translations done when the documents are tendered. Rule 68 material, no problems have been raised. Reciprocal disclosure, not triggered. Rule 92 bis, the Prosecutor is apparently of the view that most of the witnesses will testify as to the acts and conduct of the accused. And thus, Rule 92 bis is not suitable. But I would encourage the parties that if agreement can be reached on certain facts relating to the conditions in the camp, then obviously we should benefit from the previous trial by using transcript evidence. And if agreement cannot be reached, then the position should be reviewed, and perhaps ways of considering -- presenting the evidence, including Rule 92 bis, would be utilised. Agreed facts, I don't know whether any of the parties wish to say anything at this stage, particularly in view of the fact that the question of the indictment has not yet been settled. Yes, Ms. Bodson.

utterances.speaker: MS. BODSON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Your Honour will remember that during the last Status Conference in early May, I mentioned a list of adjudicated facts that the Prosecution had prepared and submitted to the two accused, Fustar and Banovic. Since that period of time, the case has been changed, the presentation of the case has changed, and I was thinking of submitting a new list of agreed facts to the Defence. But I should like to wait for the decision of the Chamber on the motion for joinder. I think it is a bit too premature to submit all of this right now, in particular to Mr. Moran, because we do not know at this point whether the two cases will be joined or not. But as soon as we get the decision on the motion for joinder, we will hold a meeting with the three Defence counsel. If there are no positive results following this meeting, then we will submit a motion for judicial notice within the relevant regulations. I should like to raise one more issue regarding the disclosure of evidence of Mr. Knezevic because I have not heard the answer of Mr. Moran as to how we should disclose to him the evidence that is ready. I don't know what modalities he wishes to use in this case. We just heard Mr. Knezevic regarding the assignment of counsel, Mr. Moran. But I still don't know what to do. I should like to have an answer to this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Moran is counsel of record, and an issue has been raised, and that is going to be settled by the Chamber. Until it is settled, he is counsel, so you will deal with him. And as to the modalities, no doubt you can discuss that with him informally.

utterances.speaker: MS. BODSON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The length of the trial, I think on the last occasion, the Prosecutor had indicated three to four weeks, based on 20 witnesses at one per day. Might be a little change in that, but nothing very significant. That completes my list. But I ask whether any counsel would have any other matter to raise at this time, before I call on the accused.

utterances.speaker: MS. BODSON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with your permission, it seems to me that the length of the trial that you have just indicated, three to four weeks with three accused is somewhat short. I think it would take approximately six weeks to two months. But this is just an estimate of mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, well all these matters can be better determined after the joinder issue. Can I ask then the accused Banovic whether there is any matter relating to your mental or physical condition, or indeed any other matter that you wish to raise. You've already raised the question of counsel, so, you don't need to mention that again. Is there another matter that you wish to raise, Mr. Banovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't have any other matter to raise at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Fustar, is there any matter that you wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED FUSTAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is nothing I wish to raise at this point in time. So far everything has been good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And Mr. Knezevic. And the reference I made earlier should have been to you in relation to the question of counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said I didn't want Mr. Moran to represent me. And that is all I wish to say at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are already seised of that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just raise one matter in relation to Mr. Knezevic. We noticed that in the Status Conference listed in the Gruban case, Mr. Knezevic's name does not appear. We take it that's a mistake because he should be present.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, he has been informed and both the counsel and accused will be present.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That matter is settled. The last matter is the date of the next Status Conference. That, too, will to a certain extent will be influenced by a decision on the joinder issue. But a date would have to be fixed, and that is no later than the 28th of December to comply with the rules. And I'd like to indicate that the date would be Monday, the 16th of November, for the next -- 16th of December, Monday the 16th of December, for the next Status Conference. If there is no other issue, then the hearing is adjourned. Senior legal officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And for those of you who will be involved in the next hearing, we'll resume at 25 minutes to four.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
